name: Power Law of Practice
axiom: Task time falls as a power of practice repetitions: steep early gains, then diminishing returns.
trigger: A workflow someone uses every day takes as long in month six as it did in week one.

checklist.text: Keep frequent actions in one fixed place so repetition trains aim instead of search.
Give daily paths keyboard shortcuts and let the interface remember recent choices.
Make the fastest route the default, not something found in settings.
Measure time-on-task for repeat workflows; a flat curve means the interface blocks practice.

antiPattern.violation: A ticketing tool moves its main action each release, so agents relearn the target every quarter.
antiPattern.remediation: The primary action keeps one position and gains a shortcut once an agent repeats it.

parametricParams.caption: STEEP EARLY GAINS, THEN DIMINISHING RETURNS

academicOrigin.title: Mechanisms of Skill Acquisition and the Law of Practice
academicOrigin.publication: In J. R. Anderson (Ed.), Cognitive Skills and Their Acquisition, Lawrence Erlbaum Associates, Hillsdale, NJ
